In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the EU needs to develop a policy on credit data, and that this policy should be supported by a harmonised legal and institutional framework, and by the establishment of a European Data Brokers system, to be used by all the stakeholders in the retail financial market, and for the purposes of consumer protection, prudential supervision, and economic policy.
the EU needs a comprehensive and detailed legal framework to regulate the processing, sharing and use of consumer data in the financial services sector.
there are many reasons to believe that the EU should take action on the matter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EU should establish a harmonized framework for the processing of consumer data, including the establishment of an EU-wide data broker.
the EU should adopt a comprehensive data policy for the retail financial markets that is consistent with its internal market and financial stability policies.
the EU should adopt a common data infrastructure for creditworthiness and consumer credit data that is harmonised at EU level, but that also allows for national variations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EU should not only address the challenges posed by new technologies in the credit markets, but also the ones posed by the lack of common practices in the processing and sharing of consumer data.
the use of consumer credit data in Europe is a policy and legal conundrum.
, in the EU, consumer finance and the banking sector are still largely disconnected, and the use of credit data is not a common practice.
